clue.text: Veteran sailor has cash provided by Captain and crew

indicators.note: the cash comes after, supplied by, the captain-and-crew pieces

parts.note: a ship's captain is its master
to crew a vessel is to man it
ready, or the readies, is slang for cash

explanation.surface: An old seaman has money supplied by his skipper and shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Marryat's 1841 children's novel is named after its old seaman hero, who shepherds a shipwrecked family.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Marryat's novel is an elderly, experienced seaman.

clue.text: Nursemaid collecting a tax for a powerful leader

indicators.note: the nursemaid gathers the other pieces inside herself

parts.note: an ayah is a nursemaid in India
a toll is a charge or tax for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A nanny gathers a levy on behalf of a mighty ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Shia cleric, such as Iran's supreme one, wields great religious and political power.

clue.text: Article on computers penned by aristocrat's literary family

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: the computers piece is enclosed, as in a pen, by the aristocrat's piece

parts.note: a swell is a toff or aristocrat; the possessive gives a final S
IT, information technology, means computers

explanation.surface: A piece about computing was written by a nobleman from a bookish clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing; here it means shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell were three writing siblings of an English aristocratic household.

clue.text: Santayana's area of truth, true by miles

parts.note: real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: A philosopher's domain of truth is true by a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: George Santayana's philosophical work Realms of Being includes The Realm of Truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Santayana divided being into separate domains, one of them devoted to truth.

clue.text: Chekhov I associate with Miss Drabble

parts.note: Anton is Chekhov's first name
A is an abbreviation for associate, as in degree titles

explanation.surface: Someone links the Russian playwright with a female novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: A. S. Byatt was born Antonia Drabble, sister of the novelist Margaret Drabble.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist A. S. Byatt's maiden name and forename made her a Drabble sister.

clue.text: President's jumper's velvet worn without a top

parts.note: a roo, kangaroo, is a jumper; the possessive gives a final S

indicators.note: worn as in battered out of shape, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the first letter of the word velvet is dropped

explanation.surface: A head of state's sweater is velvet, worn with no top layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a top' drops V from VELVET to leave ELVET, which 'worn' rearranges into EVELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. both held the office of US president.

clue.text: What Father Brown may have adopted during sacerdotal business

definitions.text: What Father Brown may have adopted

indicators.note: the answer occurs within the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A priest-detective takes on something in the course of church affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Brown is G. K. Chesterton's priest detective; 'adopted' means put on, as clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A white linen vestment is worn by a Catholic priest saying Mass.

clue.text: Herb tea for Fairoaks author mostly before afternoon

indicators.note: the author piece comes before the afternoon piece
most of the name is used, its final letter cut

parts.note: Frank Yerby wrote the novel Fairoaks
A is short for afternoon, as in p.m. and a.m. listings

explanation.surface: An infusion for a novelist, served mostly before the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate, the South American herbal infusion, goes by this Spanish name.

clue.text: Macbeth, say, at start of play's cunning in pursuit of title

indicators.note: the play-and-cunning pieces follow after the title piece

parts.note: a title is a name

indicators.note: only the opening letter of play's is taken

parts.note: art can mean craft or cunning

explanation.surface: Macbeth's craft at the start of the drama is to chase a royal title.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth is literally after a title, the crown, so the surface fits the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role is the character after whom a play is named, as Macbeth is.

clue.text: One of three OBEs distributed, right?

indicators.note: handed out in a new arrangement, so the letters of OBEs are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether one of three honours was given out properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The three are the Sitwell siblings, as in other clues in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the trio of Sitwell writers, with his sister and younger brother.

clue.text: Norse God who sounds restrained

indicators.note: the god's name is said like the word for restrained

parts.note: low-key means restrained or understated

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian deity seems to be subdued.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the trickster god is anything but restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: The shape-shifting trickster belongs to the Norse pantheon.

clue.text: Poet, chap slated badly by Moscow's leader

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: the word slated is rendered badly, so its letters are rearranged
the leader of Moscow is its first letter

explanation.surface: A versifier was harshly criticised by the head of the Kremlin.
explanation.walkthrough: Osip Mandelstam was persecuted by Stalin, so the surface is historically apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Osip Mandelstam was a Russian poet who died in the Gulag.

clue.text: Deception surrounding a heartless short-story writer, one of three

indicators.note: the deception piece goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a sell is a hoax or deception

indicators.note: the central letter of the writer's name is removed

parts.note: John Cheever was an American short-story writer

explanation.surface: A con trick encloses a cold-hearted fiction writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle E from CHEEVER to give CHEVER; SELL then surrounds A + CHEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the youngest of the trio of Sitwell siblings who all wrote.

clue.text: Glare at the condition of e. e. cummings's typography

parts.note: to lower, or lour, is to scowl or glare
a case is a state or condition

explanation.surface: Someone scowls at the state of a poet's printing style.
explanation.walkthrough: e. e. cummings famously avoided capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet used small, uncapitalised letters throughout his printed verse.

clue.text: Corrupt evil raper probably won't get it

definitions.text: Corrupt evil raper probably won't get it

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters of the next two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A depraved criminal is unlikely to be granted clemency.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and a description of what such a criminal would be denied.
explanation.definitionFit: A pardon or stay of punishment is what a convict hopes for and this one is denied.

clue.text: Revolutionary scoundrel, base

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A rebel is a low and contemptible rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kent rebellion of 1450 and appears in Shakespeare's Henry VI Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Cade led an uprising against Henry VI.

clue.text: "Commit a thing so monstrous to - / So many folds of favour" (King Lear)

definitions.text: "Commit a thing so monstrous to - / So many folds of favour" (King Lear)

parts.words: "Commit a thing so monstrous to - / So many folds of favour" (King Lear)
parts.note: France's words in the first scene of King Lear, wondering at Lear stripping Cordelia of his love; the gap needs a verb meaning to take apart

explanation.definitionFit: In context the missing verb means to strip away or take apart layers of affection.

clue.text: In which a lad featured in Romany Rye

definitions.text: In which a lad featured in Romany Rye

indicators.note: the word sits within the letters of which a lad

explanation.surface: A boy appears in George Borrow's novel of Gypsy life.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow's Romany Rye uses the Romani word for a lad or fellow, and here that word lies inside 'which a lad'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Romani, as recorded by Borrow, the word means a fellow or young man.

clue.text: Gentileschi, for instance, isn't commonly covered by newspapers

indicators.note: the colloquial piece is enclosed by the newspapers piece

parts.note: the press means newspapers
ain't is the common, colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: An Italian artist is said not to be reported much in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Artemisia Gentileschi was a celebrated Baroque painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia Gentileschi was a female painter, an old word for a woman artist.

clue.text: Like Macbeth's tale or Myshkin's?

parts.note: Macbeth calls life a tale told by a fool of a kind, and Prince Myshkin is Dostoevsky's title character in a novel about such a simpleton

explanation.definitionFit: Both allusions point to foolishness: Shakespeare's tale told by a fool and Dostoevsky's holy fool.

clue.text: Translate into Latin "girl in charge is in church"

indicators.note: the girl, in-charge and is pieces all go inside the church piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone renders a phrase in Latin about a girl running a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to 'in charge'; the second is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To render something in the style or language of the ancient classics, such as Latin.

clue.text: Heels over where Lancelot may have jousted

definitions.meaning: a ship that heels over leans to one side
the enclosed arena for medieval tournaments

explanation.definitionFit: A ship tilts in that way, and tournament jousting took place in that enclosure.

clue.text: One of three I'd taken aback in the broadcast

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed inside the scattered piece
broadcast as in scattered, so the letters of the word the are rearranged
aback means backwards, so the letters of I'd are reversed

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: One of three people was startled by the radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns I'd round and 'broadcast' scrambles 'the', giving ETH around the reversal. The three are again the Sitwell siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the eldest of the trio of Sitwell siblings, all writers.

clue.text: One who got into a mess by purchasing one

definitions.text: One who got into a mess by purchasing one

parts.words: One who got into a mess by purchasing one
parts.note: in Genesis a hungry brother traded his birthright for a mess of pottage; the surface suggests trouble rather than a dish of food

explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical elder twin sold his birthright to his brother Jacob for a bowl of stew.

clue.text: One of the "Big Three", so I am constituted we hear

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken and heard as the writer's surname

parts.note: as I'm of, meaning that is what I am made of

explanation.surface: Someone says this is simply how they are made.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Three of golden-age science fiction are Asimov, Clarke and Heinlein.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov is ranked with Clarke and Heinlein among the great science-fiction writers.

clue.text: Graduate, last of three in West

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

indicators.note: only the final letter of three is taken

explanation.surface: A graduate finishes third out west.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the actress Mae West's forename.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the film star West, famed for her innuendo.

clue.text: Tourgée's royal gentleman, one deserting French queen

indicators.note: the one piece leaves the queen's name

parts.note: Marie Antoinette was queen of France
an means one

explanation.surface: An American writer's noble hero abandons a French queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Albion Tourgée's novel Toinette was reissued as A Royal Gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourgée's novel bore this title before being retitled A Royal Gentleman.

clue.text: "Miss Whitefield tracked you at every stopping place: she is a regular —" (Man and Superman)

definitions.text: "Miss Whitefield tracked you at every stopping place: she is a regular —" (Man and Superman)

parts.words: "Miss Whitefield tracked you at every stopping place: she is a regular —" (Man and Superman)
parts.note: a line from Shaw's play in which Ann Whitefield's pursuit of Tanner is likened to the work of a famous fictional detective

explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's detective is the byword for someone who tracks a quarry down.
